external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store who is vouched for by the franchise's identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
external_entities.notes: The source does not state which franchise colleagues the identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider operated by the franchise that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The source does not identify the provider or state which colleagues it is allowed to vouch for.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies colleague and group-membership changes overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: A broker on the corporate network that signs colleagues in, issues signed tokens, and supports token verification and directory synchronization.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: Nothing calls back to the broker to ask whether a colleague is still allowed in. Group changes and leaver removal occur once a night. Tokens are good for twelve hours and there is no way to pull one back before it expires. The source does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application on the corporate network that allows a holder of a token containing the store-manager group to change prices and void transactions for every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications. It also runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker to sign tokens for every application.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_stores.notes: The source does not state whether the key store is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: The source does not state whether the directory is encrypted where it sits.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the identity broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route. The source does not state whether the log is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying the colleague's staff id and group list

data_flows.name: vouch for colleague
data_flows.description: A franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
data_flows.data_description: A sign-in assertion for a franchise colleague

data_flows.name: authorize actions
data_flows.description: A colleague presents a token to the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the broker's signing key.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: The public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker reads the signing key from the key store to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: maintain directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains its directory of colleagues and groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The identity broker pulls colleague and group-membership changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state whether this covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The directory's classification is confidential because it holds colleague identities and group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory contains colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store's classification is confidential because it holds a token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds the signing key used to sign tokens.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log's classification is confidential because sign-in records can identify colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the audit log contains sign-ins.
